meta.title: Enable constant register reuse in VM
meta.body_summary: Reuse constant registers in VM compiler to avoid re-emitting repeated constants, reducing IR output size; update TPC-H q22 IR reference.

perf_labels.notes: Single-commit VM compiler optimization with test output update; self-merged in 19 seconds without review or performance metrics.

change_scale_vs_repository.interpretation: At 467 changed lines, this is a small-to-medium change by absolute volume, with the bulk (429 lines) in a test reference file update. The core VM change is only 38 lines. This fits a small-step, quick-merge performance optimization PR and is consistent with the rapid, unreviewed merge.

review_details.performance_claim: Reusing constant registers reduces IR output size by avoiding re-emitting repeated constants.

capability_boundary.boundary_notes: The change modifies VM compiler internals (constant register management) and a benchmark reference file; the agent could produce a correct optimization with test acceptance without human review.

maintainer_practices.reproducibility_notes: Test command with -update updates the IR output; the PR includes the updated q22.ir.out, suggesting local verification.
maintainer_practices.regression_detail: No regressions were reported; the PR merged immediately without discussion.

core_change_summary.description: In runtime/vm/vm.go, the VM compiler logic was modified to reuse constant registers when encountering the same constant value, preventing duplicate register allocation. The test reference file tests/dataset/tpc-h/out/q22.ir.out was updated to reflect the reduced IR output.
core_change_summary.secondary_note: The IR output file update shows the effect of the optimization on a large query benchmark, but is a test reference rather than a primary code change.
change_trajectory: Single commit modifies vm.go to implement constant register reuse and updates q22.ir.out accordingly.

collaboration_trajectory: PR opened and merged by the same author (tamnd) within 19 seconds; labeled 'codex' by bot; no human review or discussion.
